$comment: Golden test cases for the profit-v1 calculation policy.
PURPOSE: these are the highest-value tests in the project. They are the only
thing that proves the new system reproduces the numbers the business already
trusts. Fill the `expected` blocks from your existing spreadsheet BEFORE
implementing the calculation, so the spreadsheet is the oracle rather than
the code.
If a real order disagrees with profit-v1, do not adjust the test. Find out
which one is wrong. That disagreement is the single most valuable signal you
will get during the rebuild, and it is cheap in week four and expensive in
month four.
All amounts are decimal strings. Never floats.
profit-v1: exact decimal arithmetic, one half-up rounding at the end only.

cases.name: Straightforward complete order
cases.note: Baseline. Every component known, no refunds, single unit.

cases.name: Quantity greater than one, warehouse cost applied once
cases.note: BR-04 and US-010 AC-03: warehouse is per ORDER, never per unit. A naive implementation multiplies it by quantity. This case catches that.

cases.name: Both label costs present and additive
cases.note: Labels are ADDITIVE, not alternatives. Both are summed and no exception is raised.

cases.name: Unknown component yields incomplete, never zero
cases.note: THE most important case. A missing cost must withhold the number and name what is missing. An implementation that coalesces to zero returns a confident wrong profit and will pass almost every other test.

cases.name: Explicit zero is known and does not break completeness
cases.note: US-008 AC-03: a saved zero differs from a blank. This case and GP-04 must not behave the same way.

cases.name: Rounding is applied once, at the end
cases.note: Components chosen so that per-step rounding gives a different answer than single final rounding. If your implementation rounds intermediates, this case fails.

expected.$note: FILL FROM YOUR OWN DECIMAL IMPLEMENTATION, then freeze. Verify by hand once.

cases.name: Zero total cost makes ROI unavailable, not infinity
cases.note: US-013 AC-03: division by zero must produce Unavailable. Not 0, not null-as-zero, not Infinity, not a crash.

cases.name: Settled profit with full coverage
cases.note: Settled Walmart values replace estimated ones. Manual costs are unchanged.

cases.name: Refund without recorded recovery is incomplete
cases.note: refund-v1: buying cost is net of a MANUALLY recorded recovery. Until it is recorded the figure is withheld. An implementation assuming zero recovery returns a wrong, confident loss.

cases.name: Refund with recorded partial recovery
cases.note: Recovery of 18.00 against a buying cost of 22.00 leaves 4.00 of unrecovered product cost.

cases.name: Cancelled order has zero revenue and keeps incurred costs
cases.note: refund-v1: a cancellation that cost money is a real loss and must appear as one. The imported selling amount does not contribute because Walmart never pays it.

cases.name: Partial coverage yields settled-to-date, never final
cases.note: settlement-v1: partial coverage must be labelled and must never be presented as a final settled profit.

$comment: ADD AT LEAST 20 REAL ORDERS FROM YOUR SPREADSHEET HERE before shipping
the costing slice. Pick a deliberate spread:
- a few ordinary orders
- at least one multi-quantity order
- at least one with both label types
- at least one refunded order
- at least one cancelled order
- the order with the largest profit and the one with the largest loss
- any order whose number you have ever argued about
If profit-v1 cannot reproduce these, the rebuild has a problem worth
finding now rather than after the close workflow is built on top of it.
